reasoning: The PKGBUILD follows standard AUR practices: git source pinned to tag v$pkgver with SKIP checksum (normal for VCS sources), straightforward build using bun to install dependencies and compile the application, and standard installation of binaries/assets. No malicious code, obfuscated commands, or suspicious network operations detected. The build process fetching npm dependencies via bun is expected for a JavaScript project, not an injection. All reviewed files (LICENSE, .SRCINFO, PKGBUILD, REUSE.toml, desktop entry) contain only standard metadata or benign content.
disagreement_analysis: Disagreements were caused by tool errors, not security concerns. Report 1 (qwen) had an HTTP 400 API error on LICENSE (though it was re-reviewed successfully), Report 3 (openrouter, advisory-only) had a parsing error on PKGBUILD when the model returned an unparseable format. Report 2 (deepseek) provided a clear, well-reasoned safe verdict. The underlying security analysis across all models found no injection risks.
coverage_issues: LICENSE file appears to be queued for review twice (tool bug visible in logs)
API errors and parsing failures caused false inconclusive verdicts despite successful security analysis
learnings: Tool errors (API failures, parsing errors) should be distinguished from actual security concerns and not trigger inconclusive verdicts when the security analysis itself succeeded
